findings.claim: The bakery screen became a 896-line multi-responsibility component — The changed hunk keeps a raw FlatList with duplicated numColumns/key recreation logic at lines 170-185, adds further FlatLists at lines 237 and 382, and concentrates filters, payment, reservation, order-state presentation, and a large style catalog in one 896-line file despite introducing GridCatalogo separately.

The product-card API exposes two competing quantity sources — TarjetaProductoPanaderiaProps declares both cantidadEnCarrito and quantity; the stepper renders quantity ?? cantidadEnCarrito at line 136 while the cart badge independently renders cantidadEnCarrito at lines 153-157, allowing contradictory values in one card.

Dashboard normalization replaced explicit contracts with any and field guessing — The changed hunk removes PrediccionPlatillo typing, maps predicciones as any, and probes aliases such as productoId/platilloId and cantidadPosible/promedioDiario; additional chart collections are also mapped as any at lines 486 and 512.

The new menu-label contract is partly dead and violates the Spanish business-naming convention — The candidate introduces MenuLabels, DEFAULT_MENU_LABELS, fields such as catalogTitle/itemLabel/categoryLabel, the opaque alias l, and selectedCat. itemLabel, itemsPluralLabel, and categoryLabel are configured but never consumed by the changed screen.

Implementation comments contradict the state-update structure — The comments claim a ref pattern and “setState desacoplados (no anidados)”, but agregarAlCarrito reads the inventario closure, while cambiarEstadoPedido invokes setInventario and registrarEvento/setLedger from inside the setPedidos updater at lines 280-339.
